code generation, debugging, reviews and memory use must respect this constraint even
if an upstream generic prompt suggests an ensemble. The host audits the actual

# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The diagnosis targets the trained GRU4Rec model through a host `ModelView`. Relevant hooks are `item_emb`, `log2feats(sequence)` and `predict_score(features, items)`. Sequence features must retain shape B × L × embedding_dim, allowing scores at every aligned training position. The supplied code does not show GRU internals or final sequence readout, so it cannot verify that inference selects the final nonpadding position.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` verifies that `view.model` is an actual PyTorch module and retains metadata, review data and training histories. These retained data sources are not used by the active numerical probes.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` evaluates at most ten batches of `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, with matching B × L tensors. It disables gradients and autocasting, temporarily enables evaluation mode, and restores module modes and Python, NumPy, PyTorch and CUDA RNG states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding concentration:** Samples up to 2,048 catalog embeddings using seed 42, excluding padding, reserved tokens and zero-norm vectors. It computes mean pairwise off-diagonal cosine similarity and maps it to [0,1]. Higher values indicate stronger directional concentration; approximately 0.5 indicates near-zero mean cosine. This is not a recommendation-diversity measure.
- **Training separation:** Scores each aligned positive/negative pair using sequence features, retaining positions where input and both targets are nonzero. Reports mean margin, approximate 10th-percentile margin, negative-beats-positive rate and margin-below-0.5 rate. Larger margins and lower error/weak-separation rates indicate better sampled training separation, without establishing validation accuracy.
- **Support and breakdown:** Counts valid positions, low margins and ranking errors. Category lists always remain empty because item-category attributes are unavailable.

# Perturbation & Tests

No histories are shuffled, truncated or otherwise perturbed. There are no sensitivity, robustness or temporal-order tests. Checks enforce tensor alignment and reject nonfinite sampled embeddings or valid margins.

The result contains `metrics` and matching `metric_definitions`, including the five scalar metrics above and `pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`. Unsupported measurements return null with support information where applicable.

Sampled ranking can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; repeated candidate draws measure sampling variability but do not eliminate bias against full-catalog metrics ([Krichene & Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). RecSys 2025 research distinguishes sampling resolution, fidelity to full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and alignment with fully observed preferences ([Pereira et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398)). Popularity conclusions also depend on evaluation strategy and user grouping ([2024 reproducibility study](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/33989/)). Implication for this task: preserve pinned HR@10 for selection; separately audit a fixed, bounded validation-user subset against all eligible catalog items using chunked scoring, explicit exclusions and consistent tie handling. Report sampled-versus-catalog discrepancies, training-frequency strata, and variation across repeated diagnostic candidate draws. Full-catalog ranking still cannot reveal unobserved preferences.

Metamorphic testing offers checks without requiring exact recommendation labels: a 2024 study evaluated six relations across LibRec, PREA and Surprise and demonstrated failure detection ([Mao et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950584924000156)). Proposed GRU4Rec adaptations—not established findings from that study—include candidate-permutation equivariance, batch/chunk consistency, and actual generated-predictor/checkpoint score parity. Validate probes with controlled synthetic faults such as incorrect left-padding readout, permuted item mappings, constant scores, and omitted seen-item filtering; measure detection and false alarms on unaffected controls. History shuffling is a sensitivity experiment, not a guaranteed invariant. Keep candidate-draw variability separate from user uncertainty; paired user bootstrap requires verified identities. Run all audits on the same single checkpoint per category, without score fusion or changing splits or evaluator.

Recent research supports separating recommendation relevance, explanation quality, and factual support. [ALERT (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.137/) evaluates explanations across Amazon categories and reports 70% concordance with expert judgments—useful, but insufficient to treat automated judgments as ground truth. [Human Feedback Is Not Gold Standard (2024)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/f719b8ca81221f380836e573d479c223-Abstract-Conference.html) shows that assertiveness can distort factuality judgments. Persuasive explanations and positive preference ratings therefore require separate evidence checks.

For the twenty-user audit, a practical synthesis is to record item identity, exact feedback, supporting title/description passages, and judgment status separately. Explicit rejection supports a negative judgment within its stated scope; “choose now” indicates contextual preference, not permanent usefulness; missing identity makes item-specific assessment unresolvable. Assess specificity through concrete supported attributes, redundancy through documented overlap, and prerequisites only when explicitly stated. Text similarity can flag possible duplication but cannot establish usefulness, ownership, compatibility, or satisfaction. Keep simulator traits unknown; distinguish simulated feedback from human observations. These are proposed audit rules, not validated findings from these papers.

Use supported/contradicted/unknown labels with evidence spans; manually review ambiguous cases and a sample of confident judgments. Report evidence coverage, unsupported-claim rate, abstention rate, and human agreement alongside relevance and redundancy. ## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The diagnosis targets the trained GRU4Rec model through a host `ModelView`. Relevant hooks are `item_emb`, `log2feats(sequence)` and `predict_score(features, items)`. Sequence features must retain shape B × L × embedding_dim, allowing scores at every aligned training position. The supplied code does not show GRU internals or final sequence readout, so it cannot verify that inference selects the final nonpadding position.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` verifies that `view.model` is an actual PyTorch module and retains metadata, review data and training histories. These retained data sources are not used by the active numerical probes.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` evaluates at most ten batches of `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, with matching B × L tensors. It disables gradients and autocasting, temporarily enables evaluation mode, and restores module modes and Python, NumPy, PyTorch and CUDA RNG states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding concentration:** Samples up to 2,048 catalog embeddings using seed 42, excluding padding, reserved tokens and zero-norm vectors. It computes mean pairwise off-diagonal cosine similarity and maps it to [0,1]. Higher values indicate stronger directional concentration; approximately 0.5 indicates near-zero mean cosine. This is not a recommendation-diversity measure.
- **Training separation:** Scores each aligned positive/negative pair using sequence features, retaining positions where input and both targets are nonzero. Reports mean margin, approximate 10th-percentile margin, negative-beats-positive rate and margin-below-0.5 rate. Larger margins and lower error/weak-separation rates indicate better sampled training separation, without establishing validation accuracy.
- **Support and breakdown:** Counts valid positions, low margins and ranking errors. Category lists always remain empty because item-category attributes are unavailable.

# Perturbation & Tests

No histories are shuffled, truncated or otherwise perturbed. There are no sensitivity, robustness or temporal-order tests. Checks enforce tensor alignment and reject nonfinite sampled embeddings or valid margins.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The result contains `metrics` and matching `metric_definitions`, including the five scalar metrics above and `pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`. Unsupported measurements return null with support information where applicable.

`diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds these results into instructions for a separate JSON interpretation containing `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications` and `evidence`. Diagnosis does not check validation HR@10, predictor/checkpoint parity, routing correctness, recommendation diversity or unavailable user/item attributes.
